**Summary.** The design gets the hard parts right: two explicit transactions around an out-of-transaction bank call, guarded status transitions, a lease-based recovery loop with bounded workers, a real bank port, and DB-level uniqueness on ledger and settlement items. It loses points for HTTP types and codes leaking into the application layer, business rules living in repository SQL, repeated idempotency logic, and a test suite that omits restart and DB-outage regression cases the contract explicitly requires. Nothing I found is a confirmed money or idempotency defect, so reaching PASS is a matter of the medium findings above rather than a rewrite.
